hens_rule_text: Up to 6 chicken hens (or a mix of up to 2 ducks and up to 4 chickens) on single-family lots under 20,000 sq ft, larger lots may keep more; a city permit is required first.
permit_notes: A permit from the City's Neighborhood Services/Animal Services permit office is required before keeping chickens or ducks. Application needs a property drawing and written consent from neighbors (and from a landlord if renting), plus a one-time $40 fee. The permit can be revoked for city-ordinance violations.
setback_notes: Coop/chicken house must be at least 15 feet from any neighboring residence and located in the rear yard only.
coop_rules: Chicken house must be covered, predator-resistant, kept clean and sanitary, and located in the rear yard.
zoning_notes: Applies to single-family residential lots; HOAs may separately prohibit chickens or ducks even where the city permits them.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Aurora City Code Sec. 14-134 (Keeping of chickens and domesticated ducks)
